title: AI-Coding: A Test-First Workflow for Coding Agents
description: Bilingual examples, templates and guides that connect product context, small implementation plans and test evidence for development with coding agents.
body:
Coding agents need more than a prompt to build useful software. AI-Coding makes the surrounding work concrete: define the use case, sketch the product, write acceptance criteria, implement a small change and keep the evidence beside the code.

## Context before code

The public repository contains matching English and German examples, reusable templates and short setup guides. A one-pager, moodboard, wireframes, architecture and small product requirements give an agent a concrete product to build rather than an open-ended instruction.

A fictional Request board connects those documents to a React application with request capture, status changes, filtering and browser-local storage. Unit and browser tests sit alongside the requirements they check.

## Small implementation loops

The workflow separates planning, implementation and verification. Each work package has an explicit status and evidence gate. An agent works on a bounded change; the result is reviewed against the acceptance criteria before the next package starts.

## Recent work

The 25 October update added status filtering, design guidance, architecture sources and generated diagrams using [Mermaider](/projects/mermaider/). It also made the evidence required to move a work package from planned to done explicit.

The example remains deliberately local: sign-in and shared data are future work, not implemented capabilities. This page describes the public examples and templates, not the release of a wider course or workbook.

[Explore the examples and templates on GitHub](https://github.com/sebmer-com/AI-Coding).
